item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 181138
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Sun Oct 18 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Trudy, located offshore of southwestern Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form well offshore of
southern Mexico within a couple of days. Environmental conditions
appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and a tropical
depression is likely to form around the middle of this week while it
moves westward to west-northwestward, well south of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Public Advisory Number 20a
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM MST Sun Oct 18 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 181141
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Intermediate Advisory Number 20A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
500 AM MST Sun Oct 18 2026
 
...TRUDY MOVING NORTHWESTWARD PARALLEL TO THE COAST OF MEXICO...
...HEAVY RAINS AND STRONG WINDS IN PORTIONS OF SOUTHWEST AND 
WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM MST...1200 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.9N 106.6W
ABOUT 150 MI...240 KM W OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 120 MI...190 KM SSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...105 MPH...165 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 320 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...970 MB...28.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The Government of Mexico has discontinued all watches and warnings 
for the coast of Mexico south of Manzanillo.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Manzanillo northward to Cabo Corrientes
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from north of Cabo Corrientes to San Blas
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 12 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in southwestern and west-central Mexico should
continue to monitor the progress of Trudy.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor products 
issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM MST (1200 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located 
near latitude 18.9 North, longitude 106.6 West. Trudy is moving 
toward the northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). A general northwestward 
motion is expected today, followed by a turn toward the 
west-northwest tonight. On the forecast track, the center of Trudy 
will remain near the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico 
through this evening and then move south of Baja California Sur on 
Monday and Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 105 mph (165 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Little change in strength is expected this morning, but rapid 
weakening is forecast to begin by tonight.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105
miles (165 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 970 mb (28.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions, especially in gusts, are likely in the
Hurricane Warning area this morning. Tropical storm conditions are
expected within the mainland Mexico portion of the Tropical Storm
Warning area this morning, and in the Islas Marias this afternoon.
 
RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8
inches with isolated higher totals around 12 inches along and near
the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides,
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4 inch
amounts with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the
southwest Mexican coast in Guerrero and Nayarit. This rainfall may
result in localized flash flooding, especially in areas along steep
terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves
is likely in areas of onshore winds within the warning areas.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are affecting portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico. These swells will cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Sun Oct 18 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 180833
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
200 AM MST Sun Oct 18 2026
 
Trudy has strengthened a little more tonight. Satellite images show 
that the eye has become more distinct and deep convection is better 
organized, especially on the west side of the circulation. The 
latest satellite intensity estimates have increased slightly, and 
the initial intensity is nudged up to 90 kt, in agreement with the 
TAFB Dvorak classification. The outer rainbands are affecting 
portions of southwestern and west-central Mexico, likely producing 
heavy rains and strong winds. These conditions will likely persist 
for several more hours. A partial ASCAT-B pass that caught the east 
side of the circulation suggests that the hurricane has a slightly 
smaller wind field than previously estimated, and the initial wind 
radii have been adjusted based on that information.
 
Trudy has been moving northwestward at about 9 kt over the past 12 
hours. This motion is expected to continue today, but a significant 
slowdown is forecast after that as the system weakens and is 
steered by the lighter low- to mid-level flow. The NHC track 
forecast has been nudged to the left toward the latest EMXI, GDMI, 
and HCCA models. On the expected track, the hurricane will begin 
pulling away from southwest and west-central Mexico tonight and then 
move slowly south of Baja California Sur on Monday and Tuesday.
 
The hurricane could strengthen a little more this morning, but a 
notable increase in southwesterly vertical wind shear and intrusions 
of dry and stable air should cause Trudy to begin weakening later 
today. Given the expected hostile atmospheric conditions, the 
weakening is expected to be rapid, and Trudy is now forecast to 
become a post-tropical cyclone by 60 hours and dissipate in 3 or 4 
days. In fact, it would not be surprising if both of these occurred 
sooner than predicted.
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Damaging hurricane-force winds, especially in gusts, are likely 
within the hurricane warning area today.
 
2. A dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves is likely
in areas of onshore winds within the warning areas.
 
3. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will continue across the
southwest Mexican coast between Guerrero and Nayarit today. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides along
and near the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, Colima, and
Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
4. Large swells will continue to affect the coast of southwestern
Mexico and west-central Mexico during the next few days, causing
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  18/0900Z 18.6N 106.3W   90 KT 105 MPH
 12H  18/1800Z 19.5N 106.9W   90 KT 105 MPH
 24H  19/0600Z 20.2N 107.5W   70 KT  80 MPH
